headNote:
RE-PINNED ONTO `origin/main` = `7a722141d`, AND THE ROUND-1 REMEDIATION BESIDE IT. The re-pin is why this file moved at all: peer merges landed while this branch was working (`fix/row-states-refined` and the evidence passes beside it), the PR went CONFLICTING, and a conflicted PR builds no `refs/pull/391/merge` - so no CI could run until this was done. THIS FILE WAS THE ONLY CONFLICT, resolved the way this branch's own folds have resolved it: main's copy taken wholesale and this branch's records re-laid on top - `refreshedStories` and `addedSurfaces` UNIONED rather than picked, the three citations a rebase moves (`head`, `addedAtHead`, `refreshedAtHead`) re-pointed at the commit this lineage carries, and the counts re-derived from the tree this commit ships. `head` names `6623448e8`, the commit this branch's round-1 frames were taken at with the round's edits uncommitted, which is what `dirtyWorkingTree: true` discloses - the CAPTURE's value, not the tip's. NO FRAME MOVED AND NONE WAS RE-TAKEN: the fix commit's patch at the new spelling is byte-identical to the old one in 157 of its 158 files, and the file that differs is this one. MAIN'S OWN ACCOUNTING FOR THE FIELDS THIS RE-PIN RE-DERIVES, KEPT VERBATIM RATHER THAN PICKED OVER (they are single-valued, so this branch's newer pass owns them now): at the re-pin main's `partialCapture` read `refreshedAt` `2026-09-18T20:17:07.207Z`, `refreshedAtHead` `56bbc31d9`, `refreshedFrames` 6025, `addedAt` `2026-09-18T16:20:00.000Z`, `addedAtHead` `56bbc31d9` and `addedFrames` 42 - displaced values, recorded here because the fields cannot hold both. Its `partialCapture.dirtyWorkingTree` is main's own and untouched; the TOP-LEVEL one is the CAPTURE's, so it reads this branch's `true`. AND MAIN'S OWN RECORD FOR THIS FIELD, DISPLACED BY THIS RE-PIN AND KEPT HERE UNALTERED (main's `head` was `151e53268`): THE `feat/open-files-in-canvas` CAPTURE PASS (2026-09-18). The `chat-canonical-links` set was re-taken in ONE run of the repository's own rig (`node scripts/capture-evidence.mjs --only=chat-canonical-links --allow-backend`, 23 states x 12 themes = 276 frames), because this branch changes the link toolbar on every canvas-openable target in that set - `Open` becomes `Open in canvas`, with `Open in default app` beside it, and a `.zip`/`.dmg` keeps the old single `Open` - and adds the `no-viewer-targets` and `hover-no-viewer` states. `head` names the branch commit the frames came from, an ancestor of this tip by necessity (a commit cannot cite itself). WHAT MOVED AFTER IT, stated rather than implied, because an earlier draft of this note claimed that the frames-and-manifest commits that follow move only `docs/` - and that stopped being true those very commits: the round-1 remediation and its formatting follow-up, round 2's fixes and round 3's all move `src/`, none of them re-took a frame, and `srcTree`/`scriptsTree` are re-derived from this tip rather than kept from `head`'s commit. That is a re-stamp and not a re-shoot because those deltas cannot paint the captured surface: round 2's design pass measured the URL strip at this head against the base capture and found it pixel-identical once the two captures are aligned by the known 4 px registration shift: 0 pixels differ at a >30 channel threshold in that measurement, and review round 4's independent re-reading of twelve palettes found 0 pixels above the same threshold in ten of them with single-digit counts in two (6 in neon, 9 in obsidian) - the per-channel deltas are small and palette-dependent, which is why this note states the method and the observers rather than a channel triple, the strip's geometry is unchanged from round 1's measurement, and the later rounds changed which DESTINATION a press takes, which store key it writes and what a strip offers above the read ceiling - none of which a frame in this set photographs. `dirtyWorkingTree: false` is the capture's own reading of a source tree with nothing uncommitted - the capture ran AFTER this branch's source, tests, story and rig entries were committed, so no frame in it is a picture of an uncommitted tree. `frames` and `surfaces` are re-derived on THIS tree rather than carried from the base's figures: the pass itself added two states (24 frames: `no-viewer-targets` and `hover-no-viewer`), and the folds onto `origin/main` since then have brought other sessions' evidence sets and their frames in with them, which is why both numbers move with each fold. `partialCapture` records the pass - `refreshedStories` gains the two new story ids, `refreshedFrames` accumulates, and `addedFrames`/`addedSurfaces` name the delta. The pass's own failure mode is recorded in the set's README: the FIRST attempt against a freshly started Storybook dies with `document carries theme "" after 10s` because Vite is still optimising the preview's dependencies, and the failed attempt warms that cache for the retry.

runPanelExitRefresh.note: This branch's own pass, folded into the accumulated fields rather than replacing them, and given its own key so THIS pass's record - `capturedFromHead`, the stories it wrote, the frames it wrote them from - stays separable from the accumulated fields instead of blurring into them. It wrote the six frames of `chat-run-panel/{back-to-roster,back-pop,close-from-reader}` at the two brand themes, and the SIX BEFORE halves of the same three stories live in the declared supplementary set `run-panel-back-before/`, captured from the same tree with `origin/main`'s component swapped in. RE-TAKEN AT `dd5f20e0d`, NOT CARRIED: the first pass took these frames at `68946d867`, before this branch merged `origin/main` (`647396910`), and that merge moved three modules every one of these stories mounts - `chat-header.tsx` (+173), `ui-preferences-store.ts` (+129), `chat-content.tsx` (+102) - so both halves were re-captured at the reviewed head rather than re-stamped. THE MEASUREMENT THAT CAME BACK: all twelve frames are byte-identical to the pre-merge capture (`shasum -a 256`), i.e. the new controls do not enter this story's frame, and the pair carrying the defect still differs by 463,363 dark / 457,994 light pixels. The designer's independent re-shoot at `b872ba01f` found 27 unrelated paths differing by glyph rasterisation alone and one reader frame by 175 px at max 4/255, none of which is a change in the surface - so pixels-against-pixels answers noise, while `head` and the two tree stamps are what answer whether a set is current. `addedFrames` counts the six after frames as ADDED because the before half was moved out of `chat-run-panel/` between the two runs; no surface was added by this pass. Earlier wording here said the key existed so main's `addedAtHead`/`refreshedAtHead` would keep naming main's passes; that is no longer true of this pass, because re-capturing the frames MOVED both onto `dd5f20e0d` - and reachability is read from exactly those two fields, so they say what they are. (Reviewer R2-4.)

imageExpandPass.what: This branch's own evidence: the conversation picture expanded over the app, three stories over twelve themes.
imageExpandPass.harness: pnpm storybook --port 6117 --no-open, then node scripts/capture-evidence.mjs http://localhost:6117 --only=chat-image-expand --allow-backend
imageExpandPass.runs: TWO runs. The first photographed a 960x600 fixture, which is smaller than the 90vw/90vh box the overlay offers a picture, so `expanded` showed the natural-size path and the fit-to-viewport path was never exercised. The fixture was re-drawn larger and the whole set re-taken; `addedFrames`/`addedSurfaces` are the first run's (36 frames, three surfaces) and `refreshedFrames` accumulated to 816 across the pass, which is the field the two runs add up in.
imageExpandPass.allowBackend: Passed because something listened on the schema's default http://localhost:1111 for the whole pass. Nothing these stories render talks to a backend: the picture is a `data:` URI and the column is local JSX.
imageExpandPass.reactDocgen: NOT overridden. capture-evidence.mjs's header still asks for `reactDocgen: false`, which was written against `react-docgen-typescript`; `.storybook/main.ts` on this base already uses the built-in `react-docgen`, and the rig built and captured with the committed config.
imageExpandPass.fixtureAspectConstraint: The `expanded` fixture is WIDER than the viewport (1600x600) because `check-evidence`'s ground check requires a frame's dominant colour to sit within ΔE00 25 of one of the theme's four grounds: a picture fitted to 1280x900 with a near-square aspect fills most of the frame, so its own white becomes the dominant colour - measured, a 1200x750 fixture at this viewport failed at ΔE00 79.41 from the nearest `localOperatorDark` ground, the same number the check's header records for the blank frame it was written for.
imageExpandPass.measured: Off the committed frames, by thresholding the picture's light ground and trimming to it: `expanded` is 1152x432 at +64,+234 in a 1280x900 frame (the 90vw cap binding, 64px on each side = the 5% margin), and `expanded-small-image` is 240x180 at +200,+120 in a 640x420 frame - the picture's own size, in a box of 576x378 it never used.
imageExpandPass.dirtyWorkingTree: TRUE, and the dirt is named: at capture time this branch's edit to `scripts/capture-evidence.mjs` (the three declared story rows) was in the working tree and not yet committed, so the tree hash written here is of the commit the frames were painted from rather than of the working tree. The story file was committed and then edited once more (the wider fixture), which is why this file ends with a re-stamp commit after the story and rig commits land.
imageExpandPass.notCovered: A real-engine pointer press aimed at a POINT outside the picture. The `browser` tool clicks an element by selector and cannot aim at a coordinate, and this surface's centre IS the picture; the scrim press is evidenced by the element the press lands on (jsdom) plus the measured geometry that makes that element genuinely outside the layer. A coordinate-capable harness closes it - QA's place, named in the set's README rather than implied away.

imageExpandRound3Fold.theDormantRevealAndItsFrame: Round 3's agent review (U3-1) and QA (Q3-1) independently found the round-2 fix for U2-1 to be a runtime no-op presented as the answer: `has-[[data-state=open]]:opacity-100` could never match, because the only descendant of that wrapper holding `data-state` is the trigger and that attribute belongs to the Tooltip - `file-actions-menu.tsx` nests `<Tooltip><DropdownMenuTrigger asChild>` and `ui/tooltip.tsx`'s `TooltipTrigger asChild` owns it - so it read "closed" while the dropdown's menu was genuinely open. UX measured the wrapper at opacity 0 at 0/60/120/250/500/900ms, and QA's causal control (forcing the attribute on the live trigger) showed the rule itself was live. The reveal now keys on `aria-expanded`, the attribute the dropdown does own, and the frame that exists to photograph that state - `legacy-tabbed-open` - is no longer byte-identical to its pre-fix self, which is design D3-1's finding. The engine measurement, on the committed frames, in the trigger's own glyph lane (crop 20x16+1059+79, 15% threshold): at rest 0 lit px, focused 13, menu open PRE-fix 0, menu open POST-fix 14. The focused frame reads 13 in BOTH trees, which is the control that says the box did not move and the zero was the state rather than the position.

imageExpandRound3SecondFold.theReCaptureIsDeferredAndSaidSo: THE FRAMES WERE NOT RE-TAKEN FOR THIS FOLD, and this field is the record rather than an omission. (1) THE STORE LEAKED BETWEEN STORIES - AND ONLY UNDER THE SANCTIONED NARROWING. `NameTakenByYou`'s play republishes, the stub accepts, and the app's accepted-publication path writes the listing into `published-listings-store`, which is `persist`ed to localStorage; the component that was supposed to contain it cleared on UNMOUNT, and the capture replaces the whole document per story, so React never unmounts what it has just photographed. Five frames - `name-claim-in-flight`, `reserved-builtin`, `reserved-builtin-refusal`, `moderation-rejected`, `moderation-unavailable` - therefore photographed the dialog's UPDATE state (`Update the Agent hub listing for "..."`, the update affordance, and no availability line) instead of the refusal each is named for. That is the property that was lost, and this file has no field that could record it. Fixed in `0b7aece10` by resetting the store at module scope, once per story document and before the first render.

(2) ONE WAIT TEXT WAS SHARED WITH THE ALERT. `ReservedBuiltin`'s play waited for `is the name of a built-in agent`, and that sentence is in the pre-validation ALERT as well as in the courtesy line the availability check writes - while the alert paints a 400 ms debounce and a fetch earlier. The wait returned on the alert and the shutter raced the answer: one pass photographed both lines in eleven themes and only the alert in `localOperatorDark`, and the next pass moved the missing theme to `dracula` and `monokai`. Fixed in `66983f73d`, by waiting on `which the hub reserves`, which the alert does not contain.

(3) A STATE THAT APPEARED COULD STILL LEAVE BEFORE THE SHUTTER. `settleOn` released the shutter the moment its text painted, which is too early for an answer-produced state whose inputs are live - the debounced name field, an enable flag: two consecutive family passes on the same commit disagreed about `default/localOperatorDark` (no courtesy line against the line), and both plays had already seen the text. Measured afterwards on two consecutive family passes: 132 frames, no difference outside lossy-WebP encoder noise - `magick compare -fuzz 5%` reports zero on the two frames that differ at all.

THAT MEASUREMENT WAS TOO COARSE, AND ROUND 1'S QA FALSIFIED IT. `published/` was not byte-stable: 1-2 of its twelve themes per pass flipped between exactly two hashes, with `cwebp` returning identical bytes for the same PNG twice, so it was a render difference rather than encoder noise. partialCapture.publishInstructionSetRemediationRoundOne:
ROUND 1'S REMEDIATION, ON THE SAME TREE, RE-TAKEN RATHER THAN RE-STAMPED: `node scripts/capture-evidence.mjs http://localhost:6041 --only=agents-publish-dialog` (132 frames) and `--only=agents-pull-outcomes` (60), twice each, on a worktree whose `.env` points `VITE_LOCAL_OPERATOR_API_URL` at a dead port, so no frame can quote a live backend and `--allow-backend` is neither needed nor passed. All 192 frames are re-taken. The frames are a function of this tree: every read the rig needs is answered by the story's own stubbed transport, including the connectivity probe's `/health`, which is what lets the pre-flight frame show the instruction-body rule it claims.

THE FLAKE THE ROUND FOUND, AND WHY IT WAS REAL. `published/` photographed two states: the footer's action row with a `:focus-visible` ring on the primary action, and the same row without it. Both are this app's own rendering - `cwebp -q 78` on the same PNG twice returns identical bytes, and `capture-evidence.mjs` writes through Chromium's own encoder - so an encoder could not alternate between exactly two states per theme. THE CAUSE IS FOCUS PLACEMENT PLUS THE ENGINE'S MODALITY HEURISTIC, not the encoder and not the pixels: Radix moves focus onto the dialog container as the panel opens, and this dialog's submit button LEAVES THE DOM when an outcome replaces the form, so every refusal and receipt state photographed whatever Blink's focus fixup chose next - sometimes the container, sometimes the new action row. Focusing the primary action explicitly (a layout effect, which beats the fixup) pins WHERE focus goes but NOT whether the ring is drawn: `:focus-visible` for a programmatically focused element is decided from the engine's last-interaction modality, which an app cannot set and a synthetic click does not set deterministically. Measured with the focus pinned: the same 1-2 themes per pass still flipped.

WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD. The ring is removed where it is noise rather than placed where it is undecidable. A result state focuses its own result region - a plain container, not a control, carrying `outline-none`, which `styles/index.css` names as the sanctioned case for "focus is moved there programmatically and a ring would be noise" - and this dialog's panel container is silenced the same way through `BaseDialog`'s `dialogProps`, scoped to this dialog rather than changed in the primitive, because five other dialogs' frames are not re-taken here and a shared visual change would silently invalidate them. Nothing in either family can ring except a real control reached by Tab.

MEASURED AFTERWARDS, at zero fuzz rather than at `-fuzz 5%`: two consecutive passes of each family, 192 frames each, byte-identical - zero differing frames. Five consecutive twelve-theme passes of `published`, and three of `name-taken`, were byte-identical too, which is the check that isolates the story the flake lived in. The pre-submit and refusal states that carried the same class of ring on the container are re-taken in this set.

WHAT THIS PASS DOES NOT CLAIM: that a ring is never the right answer here, or that the actions are reachable without a Tab press. It claims that these frames are a function of the tree, that the sink is where focus goes in every pass, and that the actions keep their own rings and stay one Tab press away.

why: The claim has two halves and neither photographs from the other. THE REBASE, and the first one here that re-stamps without re-capturing. `main` moved three times under this branch during the round - to `e4d074c60` (0.19.6), to `98c32e85e` (0.19.7 plus #138, which the previous pass re-captured at), and then to `c0570ea60` (0.19.7 plus #136). That move is not packaging: it adds `src/renderer/src/features/chat/clear-search.ts` and rewrites the search field in `src/renderer/src/features/chat/components/chat-sidebar.tsx` (+51/-8), so `srcTree` moved for the first time in any of these rebases, and `scripts/` moved with it (`scripts/clear-search.test.mjs`). A stamp whose tree has moved is exactly the case the earlier passes answered by re-capturing; this one answered it with two facts about the frames. The first is the shape of the change: it paints a clear control INSIDE the field and only while the query is non-empty (the `{query && ...}` guard around the button in `chat-sidebar.tsx`), plus a `pr-9` on the input that reserves the control's column and a `my-2` moved from the input onto a `relative` wrapper around it, which reproduces the same box - so with an empty query the field renders the same placeholder, the same border and the same box as it did before. The second is the measurement that closes it: `clear-search/before-rest` and `clear-search/after-rest` are BYTE-IDENTICAL in both themes, the same empty-query sidebar painted once on the pre-change tree and once on the post-change tree, so nothing in that state depends on #136 at all. Every frame in this tree of that state is therefore unchanged, and the only frames whose state differs are the non-empty-query ones, all of them in `clear-search` itself, which were taken on the changed tree by #136. The sets that carry the field besides `clear-search` were looked at rather than assumed to be empty: `chat-title` and `sidebar-new-chat` draw the empty placeholder with no clear control in all 38 of their frames across both themes, `model-picker-feedback` shows the same empty field behind its scrim, and `mentioned-files-app` is cropped to the canvas panel's own measured rect and carries no sidebar at all; no other set in the tree is about that field - `clear-search`'s own README and readbacks are the only evidence in the tree that names it. Nothing else in the tree was a different source for these pixels either, and that is measurable in the same way: 0 `.webp` differ between the head the previous pass ran at (`98b827108`, orphaned by the force-push that carried this re-stamp) and this head.

THE SYNC MERGE, and what it does and does not claim about the frames. `main` moved three times more - to `6f9bc2d04` (#140: the desktop toolchain, Electron 44 and TypeScript 7), to `4ffc3f2b5` (#139: the New chat row aligned with All chats, without the pill) and to `ad09ec6b4` (the 0.20.1 release) - and this branch was merged up onto it rather than replayed onto it, because a rebase would rewrite all twenty-two commits and orphan every citation this manifest carries while changing no pixel a reader can see. remediationRecord.designRoundEightWithdrawnPath: DESIGN ROUND 8, ON THE FOLD'S OWN FOLDED TREE, and the one finding of the round that was MAJOR. D1: the capability-withdrawn path had stopped rendering main's row box. The cause is main's `ce5fd9578` (`<button w-full>` -> `<div class="flex h-8 gap-1"><button min-w-0 grow>`), which this branch's fold kept in the ENABLED path while the withdrawn path went on returning a bare button - correct against this branch's base, wrong against main. The fix is one named constant (`rowBoxStyle`) rendered by BOTH paths, so the two cannot drift apart again, plus the test that asserts the identity rather than the spelling (`scripts/chat-sidebar-pins.test.mjs`); the scene grew the box's own check and the width check in response (`the conversation button FILLS the box around it`), because a shape-only check is what passed while the row was wrong. D2: a `--scene pins --tui-python` run against a withdrawn backend ended with one FAIL on the terminal round trip, which cannot hold where no control is mounted - the scene now reports that leg as NOT DRIVEN on the `controls === 0` branch. The withdrawn pair was re-shot with a conversation OPEN as well as at rest, in both themes, on both trees (see `pinsPass.byteIdentity`); the focus half of the reveal was measured rather than cited from the class list (`pinsPass.checks`).
remediationRecord.qaRoundNineSceneInstrument: QA ROUND 9 ON THE ROUND-8 INSTRUMENT, and the finding of the round that was MAJOR. Q9-1: the focus-reveal block added in design round 8 focused the LAST conversation row, which made the browser scroll the region (`scrollTop 1075` on a 40-conversation store), and the press below then aimed at `pins[0]`'s STORED box - 416px above the viewport, `elementFromPoint` answering null - so the write never reached the backend and four checks failed for a reason of the scene's own making. The fix: the caret row and the press row are both taken from the rows ALREADY inside the region's window (a hoisted `visibleUnpinnedRows` plus a new `whollyInside`, so a partially visible row cannot make the browser scroll as the caret lands), the caret is moved by a REAL CDP Tab from the row's own button, the pin that is read is the one the CARET holds rather than one at an index, and the region is read back and asserted unchanged. The press reads what a click at its point would ACT on (the U3 instrument) before pressing. A/B on one rig, one daemon and one 40-conversation store: pre-fix scene 21 passed / 4 failed; fixed scene 84 / 0; fixed scene with only the focus block removed 76 / 0. And because a scene change can move the pixels it photographs: the pre-fix and fixed scenes were both run against the same daemon and the same 4-conversation store, and 12 of the 13 frames are byte-identical, the thirteenth differing by 66 pixels in one `2x33` box at `1098,1531` - the composer's caret, the same box this file's `reproducibility` field records. AND THE CHECK DISCRIMINATES, by a named mutation rather than by argument: with the pin control's `group-focus-within:opacity-100` removed from `chat-sidebar.tsx` (a hover-only control) and the app rebuilt, the same scene on the same 40-conversation store reports 49 passed / 1 failed, and the failing reading is the focus check with EVERY opacity `0` while the caret is verifiably ON the pin (`{"onButton":true,"inRow":true}` then `{"onPin":true,"subject":"Pin “Sweep 035”"}`) - so what fails is the reveal and not the instrument, which is the property the round asked for. The source edit was reverted and the tree rebuilt before this commit.

The pass refreshed 71 frames and added 32 (the new mermaid story's twelve and twenty pair themes the sweep never carried), and the REST OF THE SWEPT SET IS OWED A PASS AT THIS HEAD rather than claimed by this one. THIS PASS IS THE ROW/HOVER PASS, and its change is to the two roles the current row and a hovered neighbour share: on the dark family `elevated` came down to the ladder's floor (5.0 -> 2.0 `L*` above `surface`, with the perceptual floor now asserted), so the current row can outrank the pointer's row; two palettes' rows came up to their ink caps to meet it. The assertion, the two binders that set the step and the twelve windows the binders starve are in `HIGHLIGHT_HOVER_ORDER_STEP` and `HIGHLIGHT_HOVER_ORDER_EXCEPTIONS` in `scripts/contrast-contract.mjs`, and the frames below are the evidence for the ordering.

themeLegibilityCapture.owedCommand: The owed pass must NOT be a bare sweep, and this is the trap that makes the difference: `clearSweptFrames(OUT)` deletes every frame outside a declared set BEFORE the story loop, there is exactly one top-level try/catch and no per-story catch, and the run then dies at `shell-app-shell--settings-appearance` (STORIES row 366 of 612, whose `capturePending` never clears offline) - so a bare sweep would delete the ~2,940 frames of the 245 rows after it and write no manifest at all, taking `pnpm check-evidence` down for every session. Use the partitioned append route: `node scripts/capture-evidence.mjs <storybook-origin> --only=<surface>--` once for each of the fifty-five surfaces in `STORIES`, with `shell-app-shell` split into `--only=shell-app-shell--agents`, `--only=rail-collapsed` and `--only=agents-empty` (its `--settings` and `--settings-appearance` rows share every substring with the blocking row and stay declared under `keycapsCapture.blocked`), and the gallery last as `--only=settings-appearance--gallery --themes=<all 59>`. Each of those is a PARTIAL run, so nothing is deleted and a run that fails costs only its own surfaces. THE ORIGIN THIS PASS USED, because the obvious one is blocked rather than free: the operator's own `lop serve` answers on the schema default 1111 and `assertBackendDown` refuses every capture while anything answers there, while `--allow-backend` would let a live daemon's replies into the frames exactly as silently as the guard's own docstring records. So the preview was built once with `VITE_LOCAL_OPERATOR_API_URL=http://localhost:1199` and the same value carried in this worktree's gitignored `.env`, which makes the guard and the renderer agree that no backend exists. That substitution was measured inert before it was trusted - one head, two preview builds, different origins baked, 59 of 60 frames byte-identical and the single difference identical in size - and the `.env` is still in the worktree, so the command list above runs as written. Recreate it (one line, `VITE_LOCAL_OPERATOR_API_URL=http://localhost:1199`) in a fresh checkout before running them.
themeLegibilityCapture.mixedAgeNote: READ THIS BEFORE JUDGING A DIFF IN THIS SET. The committed set is a MIXTURE OF AGES rather than a snapshot - `git log -1 -- <frame>` dates individual frames from 2026-08-06 to 2026-09-17 - so an honest re-shoot at today's tree moves the older surfaces in STATE as well as in colour, and none of that is this branch's doing. Measured at `origin/main`: `docs/evidence/shell-app-shell/agents@1280/localOperatorDark.webp` was last committed 2026-08-06 (`bb57a4080`) and shows the three fixture agents with their UUIDs, model `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4`, created October 2 2025, version 0.4.2; the same story re-shot at that head shows `Agents and teams`, a disabled Create-agent button and `Desktop controls need a compatible backend connection.`, 43 KB against 13 KB - because `/__desktop` and that copy landed 2026-09-06 (`bdf98ffe3`), and a static Storybook build answers 404 to it since Storybook's own `window.api` mock provides no `.desktop`. `chat-trace` moves 1-3% in bytes across the same span (`54baf9e0a`, 2026-09-12). TWO CONTROLS SAY THIS IS AGE AND NOT THE CAPTURE: the same story re-shot at one head under two previews with different baked origins came back byte-identical (59 of 60 frames; the single difference identical in size), and every before-half frame whose path carried a committed counterpart came back byte-identical or within 2 bytes. So: a state change in a diff here is age, a colour change is this branch, and in this pass's own pairs the difference is the palette. AND FOR THIS PASS: its two pairs differ by the BRANCH, and by both of the branch's halves - the palette (the hovered rung and the current row are the roles this pass moved) and the state the branch itself changes (`command-palette.tsx`'s active row moved from `accent-wash` to `sunken` in this change). The same-state control is stated rather than assumed: the twelve before-half frames were shot in a detached worktree at `origin/main` = `3cb1eea3c`, and all twelve came back BYTE-IDENTICAL to the committed pre-lift frames at the same stems, so main's own drift does not reach this surface. ONE FRAME IN THIS PASS WAS SHOT THROUGH A CORRECTED SELECTOR: the chat panel's hover selector described the pre-R2 flat list (`[data-chat-row]:has(+ [data-chat-row][aria-current="page"])`) and matched NOTHING at this head, because design R2 turned the row into a wrapper plus a button and that landed on `main` before this fold; the six `selected-row-neighbour-hovered` frames are therefore shot with the wrapper-addressed selector, and the reason is written into the STORIES row.

carriedRisks: CARRIED FROM DESIGN ROUND 1, NOT RE-MEASURED HERE - THE SECOND ACCENT IS ONE HUE FAMILY ON 46 OF THE 58 PALETTES: `accentAlt` was taken as each palette's own second label token and walked off its own hue only far enough to clear the floors, so on 46 palettes it is a violet-to-magenta step from `accent` rather than a second hue. A theme that names two accents therefore often reads as one hue in two steps, and the picker's miniature (which draws both) is where that is visible. Not this pass's fix, and not the row/hover pass's either - it is the `accentAlt` authoring rule's, and it is recorded here so a reader of the accent work knows before they measure it.

CARRIED FROM DESIGN ROUND 1, NOT RE-MEASURED HERE - MERMAID'S FIRST TWO CATEGORICAL FILLS SIT ON THE FIELD FLOOR ON SIX THEMES: index 0 is the theme's `surface`-family fill and index 1 is `accentAltWash`, and on six palettes the pair is exactly at the contract's ΔE00 2.0 field floor rather than above it, so a diagram's first two categories are the pair a reader is most likely to mistake for one. Asserted, not hidden - `contrast-contract.mjs` holds that floor - but tightening it needs the ramp re-authored rather than the palette, which is why it is carried here instead.

roundEightChipNote: ROUND 8 - THE CHIP'S FACE (design rounds 8's D19 and D20, from the operator's report that there was `far too much space` and that `the padding seems a bit off`). The root takes `justify-between gap-1.5 px-3` - the app's own chip step (`directory-indicator.tsx`) - so the slack is divided between the three gaps instead of banked after the count, and the control's `-mr-0.5` becomes `-mr-1` so the painted ends match (its 16px target carries ~4px of bearing). The chip also takes the FIELD's type step (`small ? text-body-sm : text-body`, threaded from the composer's `isSmallView`), because the box it covers IS the field's line box: measured after, chip font 14px = run = field at 1024 and 13px = run = field at 440 (it was 14 over 13 and 1px under the prose baseline), padding 12.00/12.00 on both rungs, and the three internal gaps 10.69/10.67/10.68 at 1024 and 9.05/9.04/9.04 at 440 - the widest band inside the box falls from 42 to 15 (1024) and 33 to 14 (440). The full-face candidates were priced by the designer and do not fit at any step the app permits, so the label, the marker grammar and the box rule are untouched. THIS CHANGE REPAINTS BOTH SURFACES and both were re-shot in this pass: the fourteen `chat-message-input/credential-*` states (including armed/masked/escaped and the four control-state sets) and the three `chat-canonical-credential-citation` states, twelve themes each, one palette generation. The transcript chips move too because it is one component: they are content-sized, so `justify-between` is inert there and the padding is not - `citation-mid-sentence` goes 251 -> 271px with its painted leading padding 2 -> 10px, which is flagged rather than presented as a fix (the operator reported the composer, not the transcript). Also landed: D21's rig row (the chip's face's own width against the box it covers, measured on a clone with the layer's inline geometry stripped, failing when the face is wider - the state the `scrollWidth` reading cannot see because the ordinal truncates first).

It moves `src/` and `scripts/` - 59 palettes re-authored, `rowCurrent` losing its bar, `contrast-contract.mjs`'s row-state block rewritten, a new `scripts/row-state-floors.test.mjs`, the app rail and the categories rail re-grounded, and a ground assertion added to `scripts/chat-sidebar-selection.test.mjs` - so BOTH stamps are re-derived here from the tree this record ships in (`git rev-parse HEAD:src`, `HEAD:scripts`). THE CLOSING ROUND is folded in with it: the rail account row's plate gained `border-control` (a row state is a step of the panel it sits on, so `elevated` against `rowHover` collapsed to ΔE00 0.00 on `arcade`), asserted per palette in `contrast-contract.mjs` and by class in `chat-sidebar-selection.test.mjs`; the remaining round-2 items are prose and this record. `head` names the tree the `after/` frames came from - it was the pre-remediation head, which is the `defect/` half, and is named per half in the set's entry and its README. ROUND 3, THE CLOSING ONE, AND WHAT IT MOVED: the SECOND plate inside a row state - `agents-sidebar.tsx`'s avatar (`sunken`, inside a row that paints `rowCurrent` as well as the hover role, so BOTH states can overrun it: ΔE00 0.44 `alucard` under a selection and 1.86 `iceberg` under the pointer) - took the same `border-control` edge the account plate took, asserted as a pair against both states per palette in `contrast-contract.mjs` (25512 assertions, one per palette per state) and as a CLASS in `chat-sidebar-selection.test.mjs`: every object a row state can paint over is DISCOVERED from the tree by an `esbuild`-transform scan and either wears the edge or is registered with the fact its exemption rests on, so a new plate fails the gate rather than shipping unremarked. Four prose corrections ride with it (`palette-contract.ts`'s `ayuLight` rung pair, `package.json`'s `test:desktop` indentation, the evidence README's identification of the tree the `after/` frames are a picture of, and which measure each 'tightest' names), § 9.2 gains the rule the two plates state (a row is a state, and an object inside a state keeps its own edge), and THE `after/` HALF WAS RE-SHOT AT THE SHIPPING HEAD: its six rail frames contain the account row and were a picture of a plate WITHOUT the ring, so all 34 frames were re-taken through the same harness (six files' bytes moved; the other 28 are byte-identical) and the harness now resolves the plate by its own edge class, fails unless exactly one element in the rail matches it, and reads its 28x28 box, 1px border and that palette's own `--lo-border-control` per frame.
